When will I receive my credentials?
Copy link

When you purchase, your credentials arrive by email immediately and also appear in your dashboard.

When you pass a phase, your next account is created automatically. You do not need to request it. Passing an intermediate phase (for example Phase 1 on a 2-step model) issues your next credentials immediately. After your final evaluation phase, your account goes through a review that typically takes up to 2 business days; you receive a confirmation email while it runs, then your funded account credentials arrive by email and appear in your dashboard.

You do not need to complete identity verification (KYC) or sign the Trader Agreement to receive credentials. Both happen later, when you request your first payout.

What happens when you pass an evaluation phase
Your account stops trading at the moment you hit the target.
After your final evaluation phase, your evaluation is reviewed, typically up to 2 business days, and you receive a confirmation email during this time. Intermediate phases skip this review.
Your next account is created.
Credentials are emailed to the address on your account, and appear in your dashboard.

On multi-phase models you move to the next phase automatically. On 2 Step and 3 Step models, passing an intermediate phase moves you straight on with no review.

Only the final evaluation phase triggers the full review before funding.

Common questions

I passed but I have not received anything.
Check your dashboard first. If the account is there, you can start trading with those credentials. After an intermediate phase, your next account appears straight away, so if it's missing, contact support with your account number. After your final phase, allow up to 2 business days for the review before you contact support.

Do I need to request my next phase account? No. It is created automatically.

My credentials do not work.
Confirm you are using the right platform (MT5, Match-Trader, and so on) and the right server for that account. Each account has its own server, and using a previous account's server is the most common cause.

Can I keep trading my evaluation account after passing?
No. It stops at the moment you pass.

At Goat Funded Trader, we prioritize disciplined and strategic trading to ensure long-term success in the financial markets.

What is the minimum holding time for trades?
Copy link

For funded accounts, any profit from a trade that is open for less than the minimum holding time is considered invalid and is removed when a payout is requested.

The minimum holding time depends on when the account was purchased:

Purchased before 6 October 2026 (00:00 UTC): 2 minutes (120 seconds)
Purchased from 6 October 2026 (00:00 UTC) onward: 1 minute (60 seconds)

A funded account follows the purchase date of the challenge it came from. If you reset a challenge that was purchased before 6 October 2026, it stays at 2 minutes, even if the reset happens after that date.

Any losses from trades closed before the minimum holding time remain and are the trader's responsibility.

This means you may open and close positions faster than the minimum holding time if you wish. Profits from those trades are not included in payout calculations, while losses still count.

How does the 80% margin rule work?
Copy link

You can't use more than 80% of your account's margin at once. This article shows how the margin on a trade is worked out, how traders go over the limit without noticing, and where to check your margin before you trade.

The ruleCopy link

Margin usage = margin used by all your open trades ÷ your equity × 100

Equity includes the floating profit or loss on your open trades, so this figure changes while your trades are open.

Every open trade counts. If you have three trades open at the same time, their margin is added together and checked as one total.

How much margin a trade usesCopy link

Margin for one trade = lot size × contract size × price ÷ leverage

Forex: 1 lot is 100,000 units of the first currency in the pair.
Gold (XAUUSD): 1 lot is 100 ounces.
Indices and other symbols: contract sizes differ. Open the symbol's specification in your platform to see it.

Leverage depends on the phase (see What is the account leverage?):

	EVALUATION	FUNDED
Forex	1:100	1:50
Indices	1:20	1:10
Commodities, incl. gold	1:20	1:10
Crypto	1:2	1:2
Stocks	1:5	1:5

Funded accounts start at half the evaluation leverage on forex, indices and commodities. The same trade uses twice as much margin once you're funded.

Example 1: one trade that is too bigCopy link

$10,000 evaluation account. Gold is at $4,000 (a round number for the example). Leverage is 1:20.

1 lot of gold uses 100 × $4,000 ÷ 20 = $20,000 of margin.
0.30 lot uses $6,000. That's 60% of $10,000, so it's within the rule.
0.45 lot uses $9,000. That's 90%, over the rule.
Example 2: several small trades togetherCopy link

Same account, same price. You open three gold trades of 0.15 lot each.

Each one uses $3,000, which is 30% on its own.
Together they use $9,000, which is 90%. Over the rule.

The rule looks at the total, not at each trade.

Example 3: the same lot size after you're fundedCopy link

$10,000 funded account at 1:10. Gold at $4,000.

1 lot of gold uses 100 × $4,000 ÷ 10 = $40,000 of margin.
0.25 lot uses $10,000. That's 100%. Over the rule.

In the evaluation, the same 0.25 lot used $5,000, or 50%. A lot size that was fine in your evaluation can break the rule on your funded account.

Example 4: a losing trade pushes you overCopy link

$10,000 funded account at 1:50. You open 3.9 lots of USDJPY. The dollar is the first currency in the pair, so 1 lot is $100,000.

Margin: 3.9 × $100,000 ÷ 50 = $7,800. That's 78%, within the rule.
The trade goes $300 against you. Your equity drops to $9,700.
$7,800 ÷ $9,700 = 80.4%. You're over the rule without opening anything new.

If a floating loss alone takes you over, your trades were already close to the limit when you opened them.

Where to check your marginCopy link

Trading platforms don't show margin usage. They show Margin Level, which uses the same two numbers the other way round:

Margin Level = equity ÷ margin × 100

MARGIN USAGE (OUR RULE)	MARGIN LEVEL (YOUR PLATFORM)
50%	200%
80%	125%
100%	100%

If your Margin Level is above 125%, you're under 80%.

MT5 desktop. Open the Toolbox (Ctrl+T) and go to the Trade tab. The line above your open trades shows Balance, Equity, Margin, Free Margin and Margin Level. Margin Level only appears while a trade is open.
MT5 mobile. Open the Trade tab. Balance, Equity, Margin, Free margin and Margin level are at the top.
cTrader. The TradeWatch panel at the bottom of the screen shows Balance, Equity, Margin, Free Margin and Margin Level.
What happens if you go overCopy link

Going over 80% doesn't close your trade or stop you opening new ones. Your trader dashboard shows flagged trades in the Flagged so far card, but the final amount is set when our Risk team reviews your payout.

On a funded account, our Risk team removes the profit made on flagged trades when it reviews your payout. Only profit is removed. A flagged trade that closed at a loss stays in your results. Depending on the case, our Risk team can instead move a funded account back to an evaluation phase.

On an evaluation account, nothing happens to your account while you trade. Moving from Phase 1 to Phase 2 is automatic. Our Risk team reviews flagged trades from all phases together when you pass your final phase, before your account goes live.

Risk looks at how much of your profit came from flagged trades. If it's a small amount, your pass stands. If it's a large part of your profit, Risk removes that profit and your pass isn't validated. You get a new account for your final phase (a new Phase 2 on a 2-Step, a new account on a 1-Step), and your trading days start again:

If you still have profit left after the deduction, it carries over to the new account.
If the deduction would take you below your starting balance, the new account starts at your starting balance.

Example: you pass Phase 2 of a $5,000 evaluation at $5,400. $350 of your profit came from flagged trades. Risk removes the $350 and your new Phase 2 starts at $5,050. If the flagged trades had made $500, removing it would leave you below $5,000, so your new Phase 2 would start at $5,000.

Goat Guard
What is Goat Guard?
Copy link

Goat Guard is GFT's risk management system designed to protect traders from excessive losses and encourage disciplined risk management.

It monitors the combined floating PnL of your open positions and is triggered when they reach a combined floating loss equal to 2% of your initial account size.

HOW IS THE 2% THRESHOLD CALCULATED?Copy link

The 2% is always measured against the initial size of your account. It is not measured against your current balance, and it is not measured against your equity.

Your Goat Guard threshold is therefore a fixed amount for the life of the account. It does not increase as your balance grows.

WORKED EXAMPLE
Initial account size
$5,000
Goat Guard threshold
$5,000 x 2% = $100
Your balance later grows to $5,136. Your threshold is still $100. It does not become $102.72.
A combined floating loss reaching $100 triggers Goat Guard.
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN GOAT GUARD IS TRIGGERED?Copy link

First Trigger

The first time Goat Guard is triggered:

You will receive an email notifying you of the trigger.
Your open positions remain open, your account stays active, and you can continue trading.
Your profit split is reduced to 50%.

The first trigger does not result in an account breach.

Second Trigger

If Goat Guard is triggered a second time, your account will be breached and permanently closed.

HOW ARE GOAT GUARD TRIGGERS CALCULATED?Copy link

When Goat Guard is triggered, GFT records a snapshot of all positions open at that moment.

As long as that exact group of positions remains unchanged, those positions continuing to fluctuate below the 2% threshold will not cause another trigger.

A new snapshot is created whenever the composition of your open positions changes, for example if:

One or more positions from the original snapshot are closed; or
A new position is opened.

Once the snapshot changes, if the new set of open positions reaches the 2% floating loss threshold, Goat Guard will trigger again.

Important: After your first trigger, any new qualifying trigger will result in the account being breached.

EXAMPLE

You have a $100,000 account with Position A and Position B open. Your Goat Guard threshold is $2,000, which is 2% of the $100,000 initial account size.

Their combined floating PnL reaches -$2,000, triggering Goat Guard for the first time. Your positions remain open, your account remains active, and your profit split is reduced to 50%.

If A and B remain open and their loss continues to fluctuate around or below -$2,000, this remains the same trigger.

However, if you close A or B, or open a new Position C, a new snapshot is created. If this new set of positions reaches the $2,000 threshold, it counts as your second trigger and the account will be breached.

WHY DOES GFT HAVE GOAT GUARD?Copy link

Goat Guard encourages better risk management by warning traders when their floating exposure becomes excessive.

The first trigger allows you to continue trading with a reduced 50% profit split, while a second trigger results in an account breach.

CAN I KEEP TRADING AFTER GOAT GUARD IS TRIGGERED?Copy link

Yes. After the first trigger, your account remains active, your positions remain open, and you can continue trading immediately.

WHERE DOES GOAT GUARD APPLY?Copy link

Goat Guard applies to all funded accounts excluding Instant Funding, GOAT Blitz, Pay Later, and 2 Step GOAT 1% Floating accounts.

On GOAT Blitz and Pay Later, a floating loss of 2% of the initial account balance is a hard breach and the account is permanently closed. Goat Guard does not apply to those models.

On 2 Step GOAT 1% Floating accounts, a combined floating loss of 1% of the initial account balance is a hard breach in every phase, evaluation and funded, and the account is permanently closed. Goat Guard does not apply to those accounts. See the 2 Step GOAT Model article.

IP Address and Account Access Policy
Copy link

To maintain a fair trading environment and protect the integrity of our evaluation and funded programs, Goat Funded Trader actively monitors account access and IP address activity across all stages.

Account OwnershipCopy link

All trading accounts must be operated exclusively by the account owner.

Sharing account credentials, allowing third parties to access your account, or using any account management or "pass your challenge" services is strictly prohibited and may result in account breaches and permanent restrictions from our services.

Evaluation and Funded AccountsCopy link

The geographical region of the IP address used to purchase a challenge, as well as the region used to access and trade a funded account, should remain reasonably consistent over time.

Significant or unexplained discrepancies between purchase location, trading location, or repeated regional IP changes may trigger a review by our Risk Team.

Travel and Change of LocationCopy link

We understand that traders may travel or temporarily change location.

If you plan to access or trade your account from a different country or region, we strongly recommend informing our support team in advance to avoid unnecessary account reviews or interruptions.

If unusual IP activity is detected, our Risk Team may contact you and request additional verification, including but not limited to:

Travel tickets or booking confirmations;
Passport stamps or other travel documentation;
Video verification or other reasonable proof of location.

Failure to provide sufficient evidence that the account has been operated solely by the account owner may result in account restrictions, account breaches, or permanent suspension from our services.

VPNs, VPS, and Remote Access ToolsCopy link

From October 6, 2026, the use of any hosting or IP-masking or routing service during trading activity is strictly prohibited on all accounts. This includes VPNs, VPSs, proxies, remote or hosted environments, and any other hosting or routing solution used to access or trade on the trading platform.

If such a service is detected during trading activity, the account is subject to a straight breach, and any payout generated through that trading activity is not eligible for payment.

The GOAT Trade Copier in the Trader Dashboard is allowed. It runs in the cloud, and trades it copies into your Goat Funded Trader accounts are not treated as use of a hosting service. Any other copier running on a VPS or hosted environment is still prohibited.

The only other exception is the first login: if you need a VPN to locate or connect to our trading server for the first time, you may use it for that connection only, and it must be disconnected before any trading takes place.

Full details: Can I use a VPN, VPS, proxy, or any other hosting service while trading?

Important NoticeCopy link

Repeated unexplained IP changes, simultaneous access from multiple locations, shared devices, or any activity suggesting that an account is not being operated independently may lead to a full investigation by our Risk Team.

Any violation of this policy may result in account breaches, payout rejection, suspension of services, or permanent exclusion from Goat Funded Trader.
